description: Deterministic NP1 vectors. The byte layout and the receiving rules are in np1.schema.json's description. Regenerate with `pnpm vectors` in this package.

x25519.source: RFC 7748 section 5.2; the input u has its top bit set

x25519Iterated.source: RFC 7748 section 5.2: k = u = 9, then (k, u) = (X25519(k, u), k)
RFC 7748 section 5.2: k = u = 9, then (k, u) = (X25519(k, u), k)

hsalsa20.source: NaCl and libsodium core1 test: crypto_box_beforenm of the RFC 7748 section 6.1 pair

secretbox.source: NaCl and libsodium secretbox test, tag first as in secretbox_easy

box.source: NaCl and libsodium box test, tag first as in box_easy

sessions.description: HTTP session; the sent ephPublic has its top bit clear.
HTTP session; the sent ephPublic has its top bit set.
Socket with binary frames; top bit set.
Socket with text frames; top bit clear.

records.description: GET with a query string and one header, empty body, client ladder 1.5.
POST with a JSON body; headers include a repeated name and a value with U+00E9, which travels as UTF-8 (c3 a9). Client ladder 2.
POST whose unpadded inner is past the first bucket, so the 1.5 ladder pads it to 576.
DELETE whose unpadded inner is exactly 256 bytes, so no padding is added.
PUT padded with 0xaa bytes instead of zeros. Receivers ignore padding content, so it opens like any other record.
PATCH with no padding at all. Receivers never check the padded length, so it opens.
200 response with JSON, on the server ladder.
302 redirect, returned untouched for the client to apply the redirect mode.
First client frame: kind 7 opens the session with nothing to send.
Later client text message, non-ASCII, no prefix.
Client binary message with every byte value.
First client frame carrying the first message itself (kind 3). The app's string holds a lone surrogate, which is written as U+FFFD.
Server binary message on a text-frame socket.
Later client binary message on a text-frame socket.

sockets.description: Binary frames. The client opens with a kind 7 handshake, the server's buffered message follows, then traffic both ways.
Text frames carrying base64url. The first client frame carries the app's first message instead of a handshake.

rotation.description: The server holds a retired key first and the current key second; the first fails to open, the second opens.
